tags.chapter_name: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Metals

question.text: Which among the following statement(s) is (are) true for the extraction of aluminium from bauxite?

options.text: Hydrated <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>Al</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi><mn>3</mn></msub></math> precipitates, when <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>CO</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> is bubbled through a solution of sodium aluminate.
Addition of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>Na</mi><mn>3</mn></msub><msub><mi>AlF</mi><mn>6</mn></msub></math> lowers the melting point of alumina.
<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>CO</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> is evolved at the anode during electrolysis.
The cathode is a steel vessel with a lining of carbon.

solution.text:
(A) 2NaAlO2+3H2O+CO2⟶2Al(OH)3+Na2CO3

(B) In Hall-Heroult process Na3Al/F6 and CaF2 is mixed with Al2O3 to lower melting point and increase conductivity.

(C) Anode C(s)+2O2−(melt)→CO2(g)+4e−

(D) Steel cathode with carbon lining and graphite anode are used.
